references.text: God's angel said to me in a dream: 'Jacob!' I answered: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Look up and see: All the male goats mating with the flock are streaked, speckled, and spotted. For I have seen everything that Laban has done to you. I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar and made a vow to me.'
Jacob was left alone. Then a man wrestled with him until daybreak... Jacob named the place Peniel and said: 'I have seen God face to face, yet my life has been spared.'

May God Almighty bless you, make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you become a company of peoples. May he give you and your descendants after you the blessing of Abraham, so that you may take possession of the land where you live as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham.

God said to him: 'I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply! A nation, indeed a company of nations, shall come from you, and kings shall spring from your loins. The land I gave to Abraham and Isaac I give to you, and to your descendants after you I will give this land.'

I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant: I will be your God and the God of your descendants after you. To you and your descendants after you I will give the land where you now live as a foreigner, all Canaan, as an eternal possession. And I will be their God.
In all their distress he was not distressed, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and mercy he redeemed them; he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
Highlights the connection between Abraham's call and the fulfillment of the promise regarding land and numerous descendants.
Links Jacob's prayer that the names of the fathers should continue in the land with God's oath to those same fathers to give them this land.
Shows how Jacob's prayer in Genesis 48 repeats and asks for the fulfillment of the same oath Moses refers to in Exodus.
Supports Jacob's expectation that his sons will inherit the land with God's explicit promise to Isaac to uphold Abraham's oath.
Confirms that Jacob's prayer for his sons to multiply in the land is based on God's direct transfer of the promise from Abraham and Isaac to Jacob.
Connects Jacob's desire for the fathers' names to live on with God's eternal identity as 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.'
Illuminates Jacob's prayer for numerous descendants through the story of how God made Abraham into a great nation from one man.
Links Jacob's appeal to 'the angel who has redeemed me' with God's promise to send his angel to secure the inheritance for Abraham's descendants.
